english: Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers $x$ satisfying $\sin\left(2\tan^{-1}x\right)=\cos\left(2\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{3}\right)$, where $\tan^{-1}$ takes values in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Then the sum of the squares of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का समुच्चय है जो $\sin\left(2\tan^{-1}x\right)=\cos\left(2\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{3}\right)$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं, जहाँ $\tan^{-1}$ के मान $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ में हैं। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों के वर्गों का योग ______ है।
solution: Let $\alpha=\tan^{-1}x$, $\beta=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{3}$, both in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ with the same sign as $x$
$\alpha-\beta$ has $|\alpha-\beta|<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so only $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $\dfrac{x/3}{1+2x^{2}/3}=1\Rightarrow2x^{2}-x+3=0$, no real root
solution_full: Let $\alpha=\tan^{-1}x$ and $\beta=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2x}{3}$. Both lie in $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and have the sign of $x$, so $|\alpha-\beta|<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\alpha+\beta\in(-\pi,\pi)$.

Trigonometric equation: $\sin2\alpha=\cos2\beta$ means $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2\alpha\right)=\cos2\beta$, whose general solution is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2\alpha=2k\pi\pm2\beta$, $k\in\mathbb{Z}$, i.e. $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-k\pi$ or $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-k\pi$.

Family $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-k\pi$ in $(-\pi,\pi)$: only $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ ($k=0$) and $-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ ($k=1$). In both cases $\tan(\alpha+\beta)=1$, i.e. $\dfrac{x+\frac{2x}{3}}{1-\frac{2x^{2}}{3}}=1$ (with $2x^{2}\neq3$), so $5x=3-2x^{2}$, $2x^{2}+5x-3=0$, $(2x-1)(x+3)=0$: $x=\dfrac12$ or $x=-3$.

Which angle each gives: for $x=\dfrac12$, $\alpha,\beta>0$ and $\tan^{-1}\dfrac12+\tan^{-1}\dfrac13=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$; for $x=-3$, $\alpha+\beta=-\left(\tan^{-1}3+\tan^{-1}2\right)=-\left(\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$. Both are members of the family, so both are solutions. (Rejecting $x=-3$ because $\alpha+\beta\neq\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is the trap; the general solution includes $-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.)

Family $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-k\pi$: as $|\alpha-\beta|<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, only $\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, so $\dfrac{x-\frac{2x}{3}}{1+\frac{2x^{2}}{3}}=1$, i.e. $x=3+2x^{2}$, $2x^{2}-x+3=0$, with discriminant $1-24<0$: no real solution.
So $S=\left\{\dfrac12,-3\right\}$ and the sum of squares is $\dfrac14+9=9.25$.
originality_note: New: an equation of the form sin(2 tan^-1 x) = cos(2 tan^-1(kx)) is solved through the general solution of cos A = cos B; the family alpha + beta = pi/4 - k pi contains a second admissible member -3pi/4, which gives the negative root x = -3 that a principal-only argument misses (way 5). Closest known: sin(cot^-1(1+x)) = cos(tan^-1 x) (JEE 2004) and 2 tan^-1(cos x) = tan^-1(2 cosec x). Different because: double angles of two different arctangents, and the second branch of the general solution is the point.

concept_use.ITF Equations: With alpha = tan^-1 x and beta = tan^-1(2x/3), the equation becomes tan(alpha + beta) = 1 on admissible branches, solved by the tan^-1 addition formula: x = 1/2, -3.
concept_use.Equations mixing trigonometric and inver: sin 2alpha = cos 2beta is solved by the general solution of cos A = cos B, giving alpha +/- beta = pi/4 - k pi, filtered by the ranges of alpha and beta.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, principal values are stated, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with mpmath/numpy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked numerically on [-50,50] that there are exactly two real roots (1/2 and -3) and none of large size (the quartic factorises as (2x-1)(x+3)(2x^2-x+3)); 9.25 is a positive decimal. key_step: Writing sin 2alpha = cos 2beta as alpha +/- beta = pi/4 - k pi and keeping the -3pi/4 member, giving x = 1/2 and x = -3.
justification: Links an ITF equation with the general solution of a trigonometric equation and needs branch care to keep the second root; numerical. Same kind as 2025-P2-Q3 (L3) and 2023-P2-Q3 (L3) ITF equations with range care.
